title: Finding the Maximum of a List with largest
description: Compare the head of a list against the maximum of its tail, and observe why the else branch repeats the recursive call.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Lines 1-4 define `largest` with the same one-element base case as `sumlist`: when `(null? (cdr L))` is true on line 3, line 4 returns `(car L)`.

When `L` has more than one element, line 5 checks `(>= (car L) (largest (cdr L)))`. If `(car L)` is at least as large as the maximum of `(cdr L)`, line 6 returns `(car L)`; otherwise line 7 returns `(largest (cdr L))`.
Look closely at lines 5 and 7: when `(>= (car L) (largest (cdr L)))` is `#f`, line 7 evaluates `(largest (cdr L))` a second time. The result from line 5 was not bound to a name.

steps.question: When `(largest (list 1 2 4 3))` runs on line 9, the outer call compares `(car L)` (`1`) with `(largest '(2 4 3))` (`4`) on line 5. Which branch (`6` or `7`) runs, and what happens next?
steps.answer: Because `(>= 1 4)` is `#f`, execution takes the else branch on line 7, which recomputes `(largest '(2 4 3))` and returns `4`.
